messages:
From: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@northforge.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@northforge.io>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:43:00 -0400
Subject: Request: SLA offset and preferred issuance after 5/27 degraded service

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the incident summary this morning. We had a significant impact during the 2027-05-27 degraded period across our EU region (roughly 11:12–11:47 UTC) and we need to start the remedy/credit conversation for our contracted SLA.

Can you confirm:
- Eligibility for an offset under the current SOW (we're on the Standard 99.9% uptime commitment)
- The proposed calculation methodology you intend to use (per-region weighted by token-hours or flat uptime delta?)
- Whether credits can be split across two invoices (we prefer to see part of it applied to June invoice and remainder as a one-time settlement)

We want to move quickly — procurement needs a written proposal to align with our internal accounting.

Appreciate your help,

Alex Gardner
Head of Platform Operations
NorthForge

Attachment: incident-log-extract-20270527.csv (csv)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA offset and preferred issuance after 5/27 degraded service

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and for the log export. We're confirming eligibility and putting together a concrete proposal. Quick overview of next steps: 

1) Eligibility: preliminary check shows the event qualifies as a service disruption under section 3.2 of the SOW. I'll attach a worked example of the credit calc.
2) Calculation approach: our standard is pro rata by affected region and by impacted token-hours; for multi-region customers we apply a region-weighted allocation (we'll include token-hour breakdown). If you'd prefer a flat uptime-delta approach we can show that as an alternate.
3) Issuance: we can split credits across invoices — common practice is to apply up to 60% to the next billing cycle and the remainder issued as a settlement credit within 30 days after audit. If Procurement needs a different breakdown, flag a preferred split.

I'm attaching a draft 'northforge-sla-offset-draft.xlsx' with the math and a short incident timeline PDF. Marcus — can you confirm the token-hour numbers for the EU clusters and whether we should include deductions for cache-miss mitigation we ran during the incident? Hannah — finance sign-off path (who needs to approve for a partial issuance) — please advise.

I'll follow up with a finalized calc by Monday.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager, Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: northforge-sla-offset-draft.xlsx (xlsx); incident-timeline-20270527.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@northforge.io>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA offset and preferred issuance after 5/27 degraded service

On Thu, May 27, 2027 at 10:02 AM Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'm attaching a draft 'northforge-sla-offset-draft.xlsx' with the math and a short incident timeline PDF. Marcus — can you confirm the token-hour numbers for the EU clusters and whether we should include deductions for cache-miss mitigation we ran during the incident?

Hi all — checked the request against telemetry. Summary:
- Affected window: 2027-05-27 11:12:00–11:47:00 UTC
- Estimated impacted token-hours (EU clusters): 2,400 token-hours (customer traffic weighted)
- Baseline expected availability for the billing period: 99.92%
- Observed availability during the window translates to a 0.15% uptime delta for the month attributable to this event.

Calculation proposal (in plain terms):
1) Compute monthly expected token-hours for EU region;
2) Multiply delta (0.15%) by monthly token-hours to get customer-eligible token-hours;
3) Convert eligible token-hours to dollar credit using the contracted per-token rate (we've used the customer's published unit price to avoid surprises).

Notes on cache-miss mitigation: we ran a temporary bypass that increased cost but didn't materially reduce customer-request failures; per the credit policy, we do not reduce the credit for mitigation costs unless mitigation fully prevented customer impact — which it did not. So no deduction.

I'll push the filled xlsx to the thread by EOD and include a column showing the alternate flat-uptime-delta amount for comparison.

—Marcus
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: northforge-sla-offset-draft.xlsx (updated)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@northforge.io>, Procurement <procurement@northforge.io>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 16:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA offset and preferred issuance after 5/27 degraded service

Hi Alex / Procurement team — thanks for your patience. Final proposal below (also attached as a PDF export of the workbook):

Summary of proposed credit (NorthForge, EU region):
- Calculated eligible credit: $18,750 (derived from 0.15% monthly delta × region token-hours × contracted per-token price)
- Proposed split: 60% applied to June invoice ($11,250), 40% issued as a one-time settlement credit applied to July billing cycle ($7,500)
- Timing: June invoice adjustment will be reflected on June 15 billing; settlement credit issued as a customer credit note by July 30 after internal audit completes.

Approvals required:
- Finance (Alyssa Chen) — approval for split issuance and to generate the credit note.
- Legal — no contract amendment needed; this is standard remedy per SOW.

Next steps for Procurement: please confirm the acceptance of the 60/40 split or propose an alternate split (e.g., 50/50). If accepted, Chloe will route the paperwork to Finance and we'll issue the invoice adjustment and a credit note ID once posted.

Alex — happy to set a 20-minute quick call if Procurement wants to review the worksheet line-by-line.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: northforge-sla-offset-draft-final.pdf (pdf)
